 Urgent Action Needed to Protect General Edward O. Gourdin African American Veterans Memorial Park  

 

Dear Governor Maura Healey and Mayor Michelle Wu,  

 

I visited the General Edward O. Gourdin African American Veterans Memorial Park today and was deeply disturbed by the blatant disregard for the sanctity of this space. This park was created to honor the sacrifices of African American veterans—those who served with courage and, in many cases, paid the ultimate price for our freedoms.  

 

Yet, instead of being treated with the respect it deserves, the park is being desecrated. During my visit in the afternoon, I witnessed individuals drinking and using drugs as if it were their personal space. When I returned later in the evening, the situation had worsened, with more people engaging in behavior that dishonors the veterans and the memorial itself.  

 

This cannot continue. I urge you to take immediate action to prevent the misuse of this sacred space. Increased security, enforcement of regulations, and community engagement are necessary to restore the park’s dignity and ensure it remains a place of reflection and honor.  

 

Please act swiftly to protect the General Edward O. Gourdin African American Veterans Memorial Park and uphold the respect owed to those who served our country.  

 

Sincerely,  

Roscoe Gay
